structure: Part 1 mined all 13 traces its read names, in full, and read both spec files (about-the-consignment.fit.spec.js and snagging.fit.spec.js). The 13 traces: from about-the-consignment, notification type (3: create new asks what is being imported, starting from a category dashboard skips the type question, plants for planting reaches an empty commodity search), origin of the import (4: renders the origin questions, region code Yes reveal and empty-code error, country optional and answers kept, country search keeps the pick) and germinal section 1 (1: create new on the germinal products dashboard); from snagging, S01 to S05 on the origin page (5), three of which (S02, S03, S04) also open the page in a second browser context with JavaScript off. Every trace is a core-journey or validation trace over the same opening run. Refs below name each trace by its zip file name in sources/traces-prototype/ and an action id from `actions`, or a request id from `requests`. Pages in journey order: (1) /create-notification, a redirect with no page of its own: with no category it sends the user to (2) /notification-type, 'What are you importing?' (caption 'About the consignment'), five radios and a Continue button, shown only when a notification is started with no category; with ?category=live-animals or ?category=germinal-products (the Create new buttons on the /live-animals and /germinal-products dashboards) it skips the type question and goes straight to (3) /origin-of-the-import, 'Origin of the import' (caption 'About the consignment'), always shown: a Draft status strip with the notification type and reference, Country of origin (a search box with suggestions), 'Does the consignment have a region of origin code?' (Yes reveals a code box with the country's two-letter prefix), 'Your internal reference for this consignment (optional)' and one Save and continue button. It continues to /what-are-you-importing, which part 2 owns; this part claims only that the run reaches it, and what plants for planting finds there. Error states rendered: the type question with nothing chosen, and Yes with no region code. No trace recorded an error. The country search runs in the browser: no data call fired while typing.

claims.statement: Starting a notification at /create-notification with no category redirects the user to the notification type question at /notification-type.
The notification type page's title is 'What are you importing? - Import notification service - GOV.UK'.
claims.quote: What are you importing? - Import notification service - GOV.UK

claims.statement: The notification type page's heading is 'What are you importing?', with the caption 'About the consignment', both inside the radios' legend as the page h1.
claims.quote: About the consignment What are you importing?

claims.statement: The notification type page asks the user to choose one notification type from a single-choice radio group (field name notificationType).

The notification type options are, in order: Live animals (value live-animals), Germinal products (semen, ova, embryos) (germinal-products), Plants for planting (plants-for-planting), Potatoes (seed and ware) (potatoes) and Wood products (wood-products).
claims.quote: Live animals | Germinal products (semen, ova, embryos) | Plants for planting | Potatoes (seed and ware) | Wood products

claims.statement: No notification type option has a hint, and the question has no hint of its own.
claims.quote:
About the consignment
What are you importing?
Live animals
Germinal products (semen, ova, embryos)
Plants for planting
Potatoes (seed and ware)
Wood products
Continue

claims.statement: The notification type page's only button is 'Continue'; it has no save-and-return or cancel action.
claims.note: The button's visible text is 'Continue'.

claims.statement: The notification type page's Back link goes to the prototype's start page, /design-release-2.1.

Continuing from the notification type page with no option chosen shows an error summary titled 'There is a problem' with the error 'Select what you are importing', linking to the first radio (#notificationType).
claims.quote: There is a problem ... Select what you are importing

claims.statement: With no notification type chosen, the same error 'Select what you are importing' shows inline above the radios, prefixed by a visually hidden 'Error:', and the form group takes the error style.
The notification type page's title stays 'What are you importing? - Import notification service - GOV.UK' when the page shows an error: it gains no 'Error:' prefix.
claims.quote: What are you importing? - Import notification service - GOV.UK
claims.note: The GOV.UK pattern adds 'Error: ' to the title when a page shows errors; the prototype does not.

claims.statement: The notification type error is returned by the server: the empty submit posts to /notification-type and comes back as a 200 page with the error, not a client-side check.
Choosing Live animals and continuing takes the user to the origin of the import page.
When the origin page first opens, the notification already exists as a draft with a reference of the form GBN-AG-26- followed by six letters or digits, shown in a status strip at the top of the page.
claims.note: References seen across the part's traces: GBN-AG-26-0RBV6D, 0PML7O, 0K2SO1, 0E56HM, 04K28C, 046VCZ, 0OXGZJ. The spec asserts /^GBN-AG-26-[A-Z0-9]+$/.

claims.statement: The status strip reads 'Draft' as a tag, then the notification type's name and the reference, joined by ' - '.
A notification started as Plants for planting gets a GBN-AG-26 reference too, and its status strip names it 'Plants for planting'.
claims.note: The reference prefix does not change with the notification type.

claims.statement: When the notification was started through the type question, the origin page's Back link goes to /notification-type.
The Create new button on the live animals dashboard is a link styled as a button to /create-notification?category=live-animals.
Starting a notification with a category (/create-notification?category=live-animals) skips the type question and redirects straight to the origin of the import page.
When the notification was started from the live animals dashboard, the origin page's Back link goes to that dashboard, /live-animals.
Create new on the germinal products dashboard starts the notification with ?category=germinal-products and goes straight to the origin of the import page, skipping the type question.
When the notification was started from the germinal products dashboard, the origin page's Back link goes to /germinal-products.
A germinal products notification's status strip names it 'Germinal products', not the radio's longer label 'Germinal products (semen, ova, embryos)'.
The origin page for germinal products asks the same questions with the same copy as for live animals; only the status strip and the Back link differ.
claims.note: Inferred by comparing the two pages' rendered HTML, which match apart from the reference line and the back link.

claims.statement: Choosing Plants for planting on the type question continues to the same origin of the import page, and answering it continues to the commodity search at /what-are-you-importing.
claims.quote: POST 302 notification-type; GET 200 origin-of-the-import; POST 302 origin-of-the-import; GET 200 what-are-you-importing

claims.statement: For a plants for planting notification, the commodity search offers nothing to pick: typing 'cattle' leaves the results list empty and hidden, with no 'no results' message and nothing in the live status region.
claims.note: The page belongs to part 2; this records only what the plants for planting branch reaches.

claims.statement: For a plants for planting notification, the commodity search page still shows the live animals wording, such as the search hint naming cattle and Bos taurus.
claims.quote: You can search by common name (for example, cattle), commodity code (0102), or Latin name (Bos taurus).
claims.note: The plants branch has no journey of its own here: it reuses the animals page.

claims.statement: No trace chooses Potatoes (seed and ware) or Wood products on the type question, so where those options lead, and what their notifications are called, is not shown.

No trace chooses Germinal products on the type question itself: germinal notifications are only started from the germinal products dashboard, so the origin page's Back link and label for that route are not shown.
claims.ref: about-the-consignment.fit.spec.js describe 'notification type' and 'germinal products: section 1'

claims.statement: The origin page's title is 'Origin of the import - Import notification service - GOV.UK'.
claims.quote: Origin of the import - Import notification service - GOV.UK

claims.statement: The origin page's heading is 'Origin of the import', with the caption 'About the consignment' above it.
claims.quote:
About the consignment

Origin of the import

claims.statement: The origin page's caption and heading are a custom paragraph and h1 (app-origin-page__caption, app-origin-page__heading) rather than govuk-caption-l and govuk-heading-l; the standard classes would replace them.
The origin page asks for the country of origin under an h2 heading 'Country of origin', with a search box below it; the heading is not a label for the box.
The country search box is a search input with the placeholder 'Search for a country' and a search button whose name, 'Search', is visually hidden; it has no label element of its own.
claims.note: With no label or aria-label, the box's accessible name comes only from its placeholder.

claims.statement: The chosen country is submitted from a hidden field, countryOfOrigin, as the country's name (for example 'France'); the visible search box has no name and is not submitted.
There is no hint text under Country of origin: the page's only hints are on the region of origin question, the region code box and the internal reference.
claims.quote: region-of-origin-hint::Check the health certificate ... | region-of-origin-code-hint::Enter up to 5 characters. | internal-reference-hint::Enter any internal reference ...
claims.note: The snag S01 is titled 'hint text under the country of origin', but the trace renders no hint there; the snag's wanted copy is not in the trace.

claims.statement: The country search is a custom component (data-module app-country-search) built from the commodity search's classes, not a GOV.UK component; the accessible autocomplete or a GOV.UK select would replace it.

Typing 'Fran' into the country search opens a list of 7 matching countries: France, French Guiana (France), Guadeloupe (France), Martinique (France), Mayotte (France), Reunion (France) and Saint Martin (France).
claims.quote: France | French Guiana (France) | Guadeloupe (France) | Martinique (France) | Mayotte (France) | Reunion (France) | Saint Martin (France)

claims.statement: The country search matches the typed text anywhere in a country's name, not only at its start.
claims.note: Inferred from 'Fran' matching 'Guadeloupe (France)' and the other overseas territories by their bracketed '(France)'.

claims.statement: Each suggestion shows the typed text in bold within the country's name, and the rows alternate in shading.
A visually hidden live region announces how many countries match, such as '7 results available' or '1 result available'.
claims.note: Also '7 results available' for 'Fran' in about-the-consignment--origin-of-the-import-region-code-...zip action 44.

claims.statement: Typing 'Neth' offers Netherlands as the only match.
Picking a suggested country puts its name in the search box and in the submitted countryOfOrigin field, closes the list and announces 'Selected <country>'.
claims.quote: input=Netherlands | hidden=Netherlands | results hidden=true | status=Selected Netherlands

claims.statement: The country list is held in the browser: no data call goes over the network while the user types into the country search.
claims.note: Inferred because the only requests between loading the origin page and submitting it are static assets (country-search.js among them) and the prototype kit's reload socket.

claims.statement: The full list of countries the search offers, and how many there are, is not shown by any trace: only the matches for 'Fran' and 'Neth' were rendered.
What the country search shows when nothing matches the typed text is not shown by any trace.

Without JavaScript the country search offers no suggestions: typing 'Fran' leaves the list empty, and because the visible box has no name and the countryOfOrigin field stays empty, a typed country is not submitted.
claims.note: The second browser context in S02 has JavaScript off (its body lacks js-enabled). The page has no noscript fallback; that the typed value is lost is inferred from the form, not from a submit.

claims.statement: The origin page asks 'Does the consignment have a region of origin code?' as a Yes or No radio question (field regionOfOriginRequired).
claims.quote: <legend class="govuk-fieldset__legend govuk-fieldset__legend--m app-eu-heading-m"> Does the consignment have a region of origin code? </legend>

claims.statement: The region of origin question's hint is 'Check the health certificate for a region of origin code. You can add the code later if you do not have the certificate now.'
claims.quote: Check the health certificate for a region of origin code. You can add the code later if you do not have the certificate now.

claims.statement: The region of origin options are Yes and No, in that order, with neither chosen when the page first opens.
The region of origin code box is hidden until the user chooses Yes.
Choosing Yes reveals a text box labelled 'Enter the region of origin code' (field regionOfOriginCodeSuffix).
claims.quote: Enter the region of origin code

claims.statement: The region of origin code box's hint is 'Enter up to 5 characters.'
The region of origin code box takes at most 5 characters.
The region of origin code box has a prefix in front of it that shows the chosen country's two-letter code: FR once France is picked, NL once Netherlands is picked.
claims.note: NL from about-the-consignment--origin-of-the-import-the-country-search-offers-matching-countries-and-keeps-the-pick.zip action 24.

claims.statement: Before a country is chosen, the prefix box shows but is empty.
claims.note: S04's 'no-country-yet' shot shows the same state.

claims.statement: The prefix is hidden from screen readers and is not submitted: only the code the user typed goes in regionOfOriginCodeSuffix, so the full region code (such as FR-75 or FR75) is never sent as one value.
claims.note: The prefix div carries aria-hidden="true".

claims.statement: The code box with its prefix uses the GOV.UK text input prefix (govuk-input__wrapper, govuk-input__prefix) with app classes on top; its hint is tied to the wrapper rather than to the input itself.
claims.note: The input has no aria-describedby of its own, so a screen reader may not announce the hint or the error on it.

claims.statement: Choosing Yes and continuing with the code box empty shows the error 'Enter the region of origin code' in the error summary, linked to the code box (#region-of-origin-code-suffix).
claims.quote: There is a problem ... Enter the region of origin code

claims.statement: With Yes and no code, the error 'Enter the region of origin code' also shows inline under the code box's hint, and Yes stays chosen with the box revealed.
claims.quote: Error: Enter the region of origin code

claims.statement: The empty-code error is the only error raised on that submit: with no country chosen and no internal reference, nothing else is flagged.
On the origin page the error summary sits below the Draft status strip and above the caption and heading.
The origin page's title stays 'Origin of the import - Import notification service - GOV.UK' when it shows an error.
claims.quote: Origin of the import - Import notification service - GOV.UK

claims.statement: With a country picked, Yes chosen and a code entered (France, 75), Save and continue goes on to /what-are-you-importing.
Without JavaScript the region of origin code box is always shown, below Yes, even when Yes is not chosen.
claims.quote: cond display=block class=govuk-radios__conditional govuk-radios__conditional--hidden body=govuk-template__body | yes checked=false
claims.note: The same in S04's no-JS context (action 39). This is the standard GOV.UK radios fallback.

claims.statement: Region code validation beyond the empty box (letters or symbols that are not allowed, a code that does not belong to the country, a code entered with No chosen) is not exercised by any trace.
Whether the region of origin question must be answered is not shown: no trace continues from the origin page with neither Yes nor No chosen.
The origin page asks for an optional internal reference, labelled 'Your internal reference for this consignment (optional)', as a single text box (field internalReference).
claims.quote: Your internal reference for this consignment (optional)

claims.statement: The internal reference's hint is 'Enter any internal reference you want to use to identify this consignment, or leave blank.'
claims.quote: Enter any internal reference you want to use to identify this consignment, or leave blank.

claims.statement: The internal reference box sets no maximum length, and takes values such as 'CATTLE-2026-01' and 'REF-2026/01' with hyphens and a slash.
claims.note: REF-2026/01 from about-the-consignment--origin-of-the-import-country-is-optional-to-proceed-and-the-answers-are-kept.zip action 21.

claims.statement: Validation of the internal reference (a length limit or characters it refuses) is not exercised by any trace.

The origin page's question headings (the Country of origin h2, the region of origin legend and the internal reference label) carry a custom class, app-eu-heading-m, on top of or instead of the GOV.UK medium heading and label styles.
claims.note: The rest of the page's own classes (app-origin-*, app-region-origin-code*) are layout wrappers around GOV.UK form groups, radios and inputs.

claims.statement: The Draft status strip is a custom block (app-dr2-notification-status) holding a GOV.UK tag with an app draft modifier.
The origin page's only button is 'Save and continue': it has no 'Save and return to overview' button and no 'Cancel and return to overview' link.
claims.quote: <button type="submit" value="continue" name="action" class="govuk-button" data-module="govuk-button" data-govuk-button-init=""> Save and continue </button>

claims.statement: The country of origin is optional to proceed: with no country chosen, No to the region code and an internal reference, Save and continue goes on to /what-are-you-importing with no error.
claims.quote: Check regionOfOriginRequired No; Fill "REF-2026/01" #internal-reference; Click Save and continue; Expect toHaveURL /what-are-you-importing

claims.statement: Returning to the origin page after saving shows the saved answers: No still chosen and the internal reference 'REF-2026/01' filled in, with the country left empty and no errors.
Whether a saved country and region code are shown again on returning to the origin page is not exercised: the only return trip saved no country and chose No.
A country picked or a code typed on the origin page and not saved is not kept: opening the page again in a fresh window of the same session shows no country, no code and neither radio chosen.
claims.note: The no-JS context shares the session: its status strip shows the same draft reference as the first context (S02 actions 27 and 45, GBN-AG-26-0OXGZJ).

claims.statement: The origin page's form posts to /origin-of-the-import with action=continue, and the server, not the browser, decides whether to show errors.
claims.note: The form carries novalidate.

claims.statement: The notification type page uses only GOV.UK components: a fieldset whose legend is the h1, radios, a button and the error summary and error message; its one app class is a wrapper round the button.
No trace goes Back from the origin page to /notification-type, so whether the type question keeps the earlier choice, and whether changing it alters the draft, is not shown.
